correctness.rationale: The primary definitions confirm that incomparable averages may have size one and that a very-fast-growing family satisfies \(s(\beta_{j+1}^*)>2^{h_j}\). Proposition 3.1 gives the needed pointwise bound \(|\alpha_i^*(x_s)|\le1/s(\beta_i^*)\). From a first hit of size at least one, the next size is at least three; the size-three case must be incomparable, and labels \(2,3,4\) cannot support three pairwise incomparable nodes, so its support maximum is at least five. Hence the third size is at least \(33\), its support maximum at least \(38\), and the later squared tail is bounded by \(4^{-37}/3\). The lower witness was independently checked: \(3,4,5\) are pairwise incomparable, \(64,\ldots,96\) are 33 nodes on one level, and the size jumps \(3>2^1\), \(33>2^5\) hold. High-precision recomputation gives width \(8.3670225\ldots\times10^{-24}\).
residual_risks: The exact value of the optimum is not proved; only the certified bracket is claimed.
